findings.description: The new optional parameter registryLine(project, isConductorRunning?: boolean) shares its exact name with the imported service function isConductorRunning (../core/conductor.service.js) that call sites in src/cli/index.ts invoke to produce the argument. It's semantically accurate ('the isConductorRunning answer') and the JSDoc above the function explains the split, but a reader skimming the signature in isolation may briefly read it as if a function reference is being threaded through rather than a precomputed boolean. A name like conductorRunning?: boolean would avoid the echo without losing clarity.

The conductor-string ternary is now a three-way nested ternary (undefined -> '', true -> '  conductor running', false -> '  conductor stopped'), combining two patterns that exist separately elsewhere in this file/index.ts (a plain boolean-to-string ternary, and an undefined-guard-to-empty-string ternary). It's still correct and short, but the nesting is a small step up in complexity from the single-level ternaries used for the same kind of string-building nearby; an if/else or a small local function would read more uniformly with the surrounding style.
